set_text.text: A wholesale markup is what a distributor adds to its landed cost to set the price it charges its accounts. It is stated as a share of cost. A 35% markup on a $22.00 case gives a $29.70 wholesale price, before the account adds its own.
Where it sits in the chain
Between your supplier and your account. The store or kitchen adds its own markup on top of your price, so yours is one step of several.
Independent accounts usually buy off your price list at the markup you choose. They tend to carry more margin, and more cost to serve per case.
Chains and groups often buy at landed cost plus a set markup or a fee per case. A fixed fee does not grow when cost rises, so its margin thins.
Who uses a wholesale markup calculator
It is built for independent food distributors who carry both staples and specialty lines. Anyone who sets category markups, prices a contract or plans overhead should run it.
